title: The King of the Golden Mountain

keywords: the king of the golden mountain
full_text:
A merchant ruined by shipwrecks was walking through his barren fields when an eerie black dwarf offered him boundless wealth in exchange for the first thing that brushed against his leg when he returned home. Thinking of his faithful hound, the merchant agreed. But to his horror, his little seven-year-old son ran out to embrace his knees.

Years later, when the time came to surrender the boy, the lad stood inside a circle of holy chalk, and the dwarf could not touch him. Placed adrift in a wooden skiff upon the river, the youth floated across the endless sea until he landed on the shores of the enchanted Golden Mountain.

There he found an enchanted snake that begged him to endure three nights of silent torment from dark phantoms to break her curse. The brave youth endured the spectral blows without uttering a single groan. On the third morning, the serpent transformed into a radiant queen, who made him King of the Golden Mountain and bore him a lovely child.

Longing to visit his aged father, the young king returned to his native land, bearing a ring that could transport him anywhere—provided he did not demand his wife accompany him against her will. Overcome by pride at a feast, he invoked her presence, breaking the pact. The queen took the child and the ring while he slept and vanished back to the Golden Mountain.

Undaunted, the king journeyed on foot for twelve long years. Along the way, he encountered three squabbling giants and cleverely obtained their three magical treasures: a sword that decapitated enemies at a word, a cloak of invisibility, and boots that could travel a hundred leagues in a single stride.

Arriving at the Golden Mountain just as the unfaithful queen was celebrating her wedding to another, the invisible king revealed the truth, drove the pretender from the throne, and reclaimed his rightful sovereignty with dignity and justice.
moral: Steadfast loyalty overcomes broken oaths, and magical gifts aid the righteous heart.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The King of the Golden Mountain"?
options: True wealth lies in contentment and honesty; greed leads to ruin.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.
